method: Chord tokens are split on spaces, commas, semicolons, colons and bar lines; parentheses and brackets are removed, and sharps and flats are read in ASCII or as the musical signs. A token is a root letter with up to two accidentals, a quality and an optional slash bass; the quality table covers major, minor, power, sixth, seventh, major seventh, minor seventh, half-diminished, diminished, diminished seventh, augmented, suspended second and fourth, seventh suspended fourth, add nine, ninth, eleventh and thirteenth chords in their usual shorthand. Anything else is refused with the offending token, at most 64 chords are accepted, and an N.C. marker is skipped and reported. Each of the 24 major and natural-minor keys is scored by summing, over the chords, the number of chord tones that fall inside that key's seven-note scale times a position weight: 2 for the first chord, 2 for a middle chord and 3 for the last chord, or 3 when the progression has a single chord. The denominator is the same for every key, so the weighted fit percentage is directly comparable, and each chord also records whether all of its tones are inside the key. Ties are broken by tonic evidence, not by harmonic analysis: a tonic chord whose quality matches the mode (major triad for a major key, minor triad for a minor key) adds 2, a matching tonic chord in first position adds 10, one in last position adds 4, and a final dominant-to-tonic pair adds 6. Roman numerals come from the letter relationship between the chord root and the tonic, so the degree number is fixed by the letters and any accidental prefix is the difference between the chord root and that degree of the key; the numeral is upper case for major, dominant, augmented and suspended chords and lower case for minor and diminished ones, with the quality written as a suffix such as maj7, 7, ø7, °7, +, sus4, add9 or 9. Chords containing tones outside the scale are marked with those tones, spelled from the chord's own intervals. The page compares pitch classes only: inversions, voicings, melody, rhythm, harmonic function and secondary dominants are not modelled, and a short loop can fit two related keys equally well, which the result states rather than hides. It runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Roman numeral analysis labels a chord by the scale degree of its root, with upper case for major and lower case for minor qualities and accidentals written before the numeral for chromatic roots.

A major scale has semitone steps 2, 2, 1, 2, 2, 2, 1 from its tonic and a natural minor scale 2, 1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 2, which fixes the seven pitch classes available to each of the 24 major and minor keys.

A diatonic progression uses chords whose tones belong to one key's scale; chords with tones outside it are borrowed or chromatic, and relative major and minor keys share the same seven pitch classes, so a short progression can fit both.

Common chord shorthand: a bare letter is a major triad, m is minor, 7 a dominant seventh, maj7 a major seventh, m7 a minor seventh, m7b5 a half-diminished seventh, dim7 a diminished seventh, sus4 replaces the third with the fourth, and an added 9 or 11 or 13 extends the chord without implying a seventh.
